types.embedding_query_text: SpaceTelescope: A space telescope is a large, complex instrument designed for astronomical observation from space. Also called OrbitalObservatory, CelestialScope, AstroTelescope, SkyScanner. Examples: Euclid, James Webb space telescope, Euclid telescope, Euclid space telescope.

chosen_type.label: SpaceTelescope
chosen_type.definition: A large, complex instrument designed for astronomical observation from space.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate accurately represents a space telescope as a specialized scientific instrument; 'Product' is the closest general parent.

candidates.label: WarrantyScope
candidates.comment: An enumeration describing the range of services covered by a warranty in case of product defect or malfunction. Also called warranty coverage, guarantee scope, service level. Examples: "Parts and Labor - Bring In", "Labor - On Site", "Parts Only".

candidates.label: DefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.

candidates.label: GeospatialGeometry
candidates.comment: GeospatialGeometry is an Intangible supertype of GeoShape, designed to accommodate definitions from Geo-Spatial best practices. Also called spatial geometry, geographic feature. Examples: A GeoShape, a KML polygon, a GeoJSON object.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

types.embedding_query_text: AstronomicalObject: An astronomical object is a naturally occurring physical entity existing in space, typically studied through astronomical observation. Also called CelestialBody, CosmicObject, StellarEntity, GalacticFeature. Examples: quasars, quasar, ancient quasars, very brightest ancient quasars.

chosen_type.label: AstronomicalObject
chosen_type.definition: A naturally occurring physical entity existing in space, typically studied through astronomical observation.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org candidates focus on media or intangible data, not physical cosmic entities; 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: Observation
candidates.comment: An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value. Examples: a temperature reading, a stock price at a specific time, a survey response. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which is a specific type of observation with a numerical value and unit.

candidates.label: AudioObject
candidates.comment: An AudioObject is a MediaObject representing an audio file or recording. Also called audio file, sound recording, sound clip, audio track. Examples: an MP3 song, a podcast episode, a voice memo, a sound effect. Distinct from VideoObject, which contains visual content.

candidates.label: VideoObject
candidates.comment: A media object representing a video file. Also called video file, digital video, movie clip. Examples: an MP4 video, a YouTube video, a short film.

candidates.label: MediaObject
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a media object like an image, video, audio, or text, which can be embedded or downloaded. Also called digital media asset, multimedia file, content object. Examples: a JPEG image file, an MP4 video, an MP3 audio track, a PDF document. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization Examples: European Space Agency, ESA.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The European Space Agency is a clear example of an Organization, which matches the schema.org definition.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: DENonprofitType
candidates.comment: DENonprofitType is an enumeration representing specific types of non-profit organizations recognized under German fiscal code, article 52. Also called German non-profit classification, AO 52 non-profit. Examples: A German charitable foundation, a registered German association for public benefit.

candidates.label: Airline
candidates.comment: An Airline is an Organization that provides air transportation services for passengers. Also called air carrier, air transport company, flight operator. Examples: United Airlines, British Airways, Lufthansa, Southwest Airlines. Distinct from Airport, which is the facility where planes take off and land.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

types.embedding_query_text: Person Examples: Daming Yang, Joseph Hennawi, Yang, lead author.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Names like 'Daming Yang' and 'Joseph Hennawi' are individual people, fitting the schema.org Person definition.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Guide
candidates.comment: A Guide is a creative work that recommends specific products, services, or aspects of a thing for a user to consider, often detailing features or providing rankings. Also called buying guide, product review, ranked list, how-to manual. Examples: 'Best Laptops of 2023' article, a travel guide to Paris, a car buying guide, a beginner's photography guide. Distinct from HowTo, which provides step-by-step instructions to achieve a result.

candidates.label: BuddhistTemple
candidates.comment: A BuddhistTemple is a PlaceOfWorship dedicated to Buddhist religious practices and ceremonies. Also called pagoda, wat, vihara, dharma center. Examples: Wat Arun, Todai-ji Temple, a local Zen center.

candidates.label: WPHeader
candidates.comment: The top section of a web page, typically containing the site's logo, main navigation, and branding elements. Also called page header, website header, site top. Examples: a website's logo and main menu bar, a search bar at the top of a page, a site title.

candidates.label: AboutPage
candidates.comment: An AboutPage is a specific type of WebPage dedicated to providing information about an organization, person, or entity. Also called About Us page, company info page, profile page. Examples: The "About Us" section of a company website, a personal biography page, a project overview page.

types.embedding_query_text: Rocket: A rocket is a vehicle used to launch spacecraft into outer space. Also called LaunchVehicle, SpacecraftLauncher, OrbitalRocket, ExoplanetVehicle. Examples: Falcon 9 rocket.

chosen_type.label: Vehicle
chosen_type.justification: The Falcon 9 rocket is a type of vehicle designed for transporting spacecraft, aligning with the schema.org Vehicle definition.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: Car
candidates.comment: A wheeled, self-powered motor vehicle primarily used for personal transportation. Also called automobile, motorcar, auto, vehicle. Examples: Toyota Camry, Ford F-150, Tesla Model 3, Honda Civic.

candidates.label: MotorizedBicycle
candidates.comment: A vehicle that is primarily a bicycle equipped with an attached motor for power or assistance. Also called e-bike, electric bicycle, moped (older sense). Examples: a pedal-assist electric bicycle, a bicycle with a small gas engine kit. Distinct from Motorcycle, which is designed from the ground up as a motor vehicle.

candidates.label: CarUsageType
candidates.comment: An enumeration indicating a specific purpose or usage of a car. Also called vehicle use category, automobile purpose, car application type. Examples: Commercial rental, driving school, taxi service, personal use.

candidates.label: Flight
candidates.comment: A Flight is a Trip representing an airline journey. Also called air travel, plane ride, air route. Examples: Flight BA249 from London to Rio, a domestic flight from New York to Chicago, a charter flight.

types.embedding_query_text: GalaxyCluster Examples: Perseus galaxy cluster, Abell 2390.

chosen_type.label: GalaxyCluster
chosen_type.definition: A collection of galaxies bound together by gravity, forming a large-scale structure in the universe.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org candidates relate to media or errors; no class matches the astronomical concept of a galaxy cluster.

candidates.label: BroadcastFrequencySpecification
candidates.comment: A BroadcastFrequencySpecification is an Intangible entity detailing the frequency in MHz and the modulation used for a particular BroadcastService. Also called frequency details, broadcast parameters, channel specification. Examples: 99.5 FM, 1080 AM, UHF channel 23.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: GameServerStatus
candidates.comment: A GameServerStatus is a StatusEnumeration representing the operational status of a game server. Also called server status, game server state. Examples: Online, Offline, Maintenance.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: HyperTocEntry
candidates.comment: A HyperTocEntry is a creative work representing an individual item or section within a HyperToc, specifying its associated media and time offsets. Also called table of contents item, media chapter, section marker. Examples: 'Introduction (0:00-5:30)', 'Keynote Speech (10:15-30:00)', 'Q&A Session (30:00-45:00)'.

types.embedding_query_text: CosmicEpoch: A cosmic epoch is a distinct period in the history of the universe marked by specific astrophysical processes. Also called CosmicPeriod, UniversalPhase, StellarEra, GalacticAge. Examples: epoch of reionization, cosmic dark ages.

chosen_type.label: CosmicEpoch
chosen_type.definition: A distinct period in the history of the universe marked by specific astrophysical processes.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org candidates focus on media seasons or time data types; 'CosmicEpoch' represents a unique astrophysical time period.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: TVEpisode
candidates.comment: A single installment of a television series, typically part of a season. Also called television episode, show episode, broadcast installment. Examples: 'The Pilot' episode of a new series, 'Episode 5 of Season 2' of a drama.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: Examples like '2023-01-01' are calendar dates, matching the schema.org Date datatype.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration is an Enumeration of modes for organizing an event, indicating whether it is online or offline. Also called attendance type, event format, participation mode. Examples: OnlineEventAttendanceMode, OfflineEventAttendanceMode, MixedEventAttendanceMode.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

chosen_type.label: CosmicAge
chosen_type.definition: A time period in the universe's history characterized by specific astrophysical phenomena.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org candidates relate to money or measurements; 'CosmicAge' represents a distinct astrophysical time frame.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: DENonprofitType
candidates.comment: DENonprofitType is an enumeration representing specific types of non-profit organizations recognized under German fiscal code, article 52. Also called German non-profit classification, AO 52 non-profit. Examples: A German charitable foundation, a registered German association for public benefit.

candidates.label: MusicAlbumReleaseType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumReleaseType is an enumeration describing the kind of release for a music album. Also called release format, album release category. Examples: Single, EP, Album. Distinct from MusicAlbumProductionType, which describes the content type.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

types.embedding_query_text: Distance Examples: 1.5 million kilometers, 1.5 million km, 1.5M km.

chosen_type.label: Distance
chosen_type.justification: The example '1.5 million kilometers' is a quantitative distance, matching the schema.org Distance class.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: GeoCoordinates
candidates.comment: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: SizeSystemEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size systems used for different product categories. Also called sizing standard, measurement system, apparel sizing convention. Examples: 'US', 'UK', 'EU', 'EN-13402', 'Imperial'.

candidates.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
candidates.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

types.embedding_query_text: MissionObjective Examples: chart one-third of the sky.

candidates.label: HowToStep
candidates.comment: A HowToStep is a creative work representing an ordered step in a HowTo guide, which can contain directions and/or tips. Also called instruction stage, procedural step, action sequence. Examples: 'Step 1: Gather Ingredients,' 'Step 2: Preheat Oven,' 'Step 3: Bake for 30 minutes.'

candidates.label: GeoCoordinates
candidates.comment: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: MedicalStudyStatus
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing the status of a medical study. Also called study phase, research status, trial stage. Examples: "Recruiting", "Active, not recruiting", "Completed", "Terminated".

candidates.label: MedicalObservationalStudyDesign
candidates.comment: An enumeration of design models for observational medical studies. Also called observational study type, research design, epidemiological design. Examples: "CohortStudy", "CaseControlStudy", "CrossSectionalStudy".

candidates.label: BroadcastFrequencySpecification
candidates.comment: A BroadcastFrequencySpecification is an Intangible entity detailing the frequency in MHz and the modulation used for a particular BroadcastService. Also called frequency details, broadcast parameters, channel specification. Examples: 99.5 FM, 1080 AM, UHF channel 23.

types.embedding_query_text: CosmicProblem Examples: problem of early massive galaxies.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskEstimator
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any rule set or interactive tool used to estimate the risk of developing a complication or condition. Also called risk assessment tool, prognosis predictor, clinical risk model. Examples: a calculator for stroke risk, a scoring system for surgical complications. Distinct from MedicalRiskFactor, which is a single factor increasing risk.
